units.function: HTTP route tests for approval decision idempotency, tenant non-disclosure, authenticated-human attribution, Agent-created issue-linked board requests and low-trust recovery-run containment.
units.dependencyDirection: Session or API-key actor middleware supplies trusted human/Agent identity; approval routes scope records to the actor's Company, call Approval/IssueApproval/Heartbeat/Secret/Access services, then emit activity and wakeup side effects only when a decision was newly applied.
units.keyDataModels: Board or Agent actor, Company scope, Approval type/status/payload/decision note/requester/decider, linked Issue ids, heartbeat run contextSnapshot and status-only recovery capability flags.
units.lifecycle: Approve/reject retries return the resolved record without repeating logs, issue lookup or wakeups. Cross-Company decision and revision attempts return indistinguishable 404. Human identity comes from the authenticated actor rather than request fields. Normal Agents may open generic board requests linked to Issues, while cheap status-only recovery runs cannot create, resubmit or comment on approvals.
units.testAssessment: Eleven route-level cases cover duplicate side-effect suppression, cross-tenant non-disclosure, forged decider rejection, generic Agent requests and three recovery-run mutation paths. Missing are requester/approver separation, role/risk policy, exact action and payload digest binding, evidence/result/permission/data-contract references, concurrent requests, Idempotency-Key, revision versioning, comment/list/read containment, expired/cancelled approvals, structured error codes and real database/service integration rather than permissive mocks.
units.designRationale: Keep retries safe, derive attribution from trusted authentication context, avoid tenant existence oracles, let Agents escalate decisions to humans and prevent degraded watchdog runs from changing governance state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs Agent-initiated escalation and human decisions that are tenant-safe and retryable while proving the exact proposed action, authority, data, evidence and accountable human through revision and execution.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT actor-derived attribution, 404 non-disclosure, explicit low-trust capability denial and issue/work linkage. Replace generic title payloads with a versioned ApprovalRequest binding canonical action digest, Work, ResponsibilityContract, Agent, permission/data grants, evidence and expiry; require policy-selected accountable human and structured stable errors.
units.responsibilityConflict: An Agent can create a generic board approval whose fixture binds only a title and optional Issue ids, not an executable action or responsibility contract. Human decision tests prove identity attribution but not authority, independence, what the reviewer saw, or whether later side effects match the approved bytes.

units.function: ApprovalService unit tests for compare-and-set decision idempotency, hire-Agent activation/creation side effects and lookup of an Agent's open hire approval.
units.dependencyDirection: ApprovalService reads and conditionally updates Approval rows, then invokes AgentService activation/create/terminate and an external hire-approved notification hook; a SQL-filtered query finds open hire approvals by Company, type, status and payload Agent id.
units.keyDataModels: Hire Approval company/type/status/payload/requesting Agent, decision user/note/time, optional pending Agent id, Adapter config SecretRef, applied boolean and post-decision Agent/notification side effects.
units.lifecycle: A pending approval is conditionally resolved. If another worker wins, the service rereads the final row and returns applied=false without repeating Agent or notification effects. A winning approval activates the pending Agent or creates one from payload and notifies the requester; rejection terminates the pending Agent. Open-hire lookup delegates all predicates to SQL.
units.testAssessment: Six focused service tests demonstrate the compare-and-set winner/loser contract, winning side effects, Agent creation from SecretRef payload and filtered lookup. The database and downstream services are stubs, so they do not cover transaction isolation, crashes between status update and side effects, side-effect failure/retry, outbox durability, duplicate external notification, concurrent payload mutation, approval digest, create/activate rollback, requester/approver policy or JSON predicate/index behavior.
units.designRationale: Prevent concurrent or retried decisions from activating, terminating or notifying twice while supporting both pre-created pending Agents and deferred creation from an approved payload.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must resolve approvals exactly once at the decision ledger while guaranteeing eventual, idempotent execution of every approved side effect and preserving proof that execution used the approved revision.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the boundary around an immutable decision plus transactional outbox/work command. Keep conditional state transition and explicit applied result, but persist a canonical action digest and durable side-effect intents in the same transaction; consumers use idempotency keys, retry independently, record execution receipts and compensate or escalate permanent failure.
units.responsibilityConflict: The current no-op retry rule creates a crash gap: if the database becomes approved and Agent activation or notification fails, later retries see applied=false and deliberately skip those side effects. Approval payload JSON is mutable authority without an immutable digest, and the tests do not prove that the exact reviewed configuration is what an external runtime receives.
